blocking_focus: Ordinary mouse-look remains non-responsive: multiple large look injections leave yaw at 12.6 degrees, preventing effective aim and progression beyond Alpha.
Two stable Charlie enemy identities remain only 0.11 meters apart, violating the required collision-free enemy separation.

Enemy shots now have authoritative shot IDs and damage, but their player-facing effect is an oversized orange octagon/white cross that obscures actors and scenery instead of a bounded muzzle, tracer, or impact response.
Persisted 200% UI scale clips critical post-deployment story and objective text inside fixed HUD bounds.
Target performance remains unqualified because the registered runtime uses Mesa llvmpipe at 1280x720 and the observed combat blockage prevents an explosion-window run.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `clean_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Restore ordinary mouse and gamepad aiming, collision-free 18-enemy A→B→C progression, and visibly distinct hip/ADS plus combat-motion states while preserving the intact arena, bound AK-74M/Saiga-12 packages, Alpha AI behavior, shell flow, and atomic checkpoint restoration.

diagnosis.root_cause: The camera and ADS paths both rely on unhandled pointer events, so shell/UI handling can starve ordinary look and right-mouse input even though gameplay is enabled; the authoritative state then never receives observable look or ADS edges. Separately, enemy slot projection checks separation only opportunistically and returns the original occupied navigation point when its bounded search finds no valid alternative, allowing distinct Charlie identities to start 0.11 m apart. These are ownership and reservation failures, not transform-calibration defects.

stop_conditions: Stop if clean boot, resource loading, or the single authored arena instance regresses.
Stop if gameplay input begins leaking through title, briefing, pause, terminal, death, or result states, or if one physical edge is consumed more than once.

Do not accept an overlapping enemy fallback; if 18 valid navigation-resolved reservations cannot be allocated, report the failing actor, requested slot, projection, and nearest-neighbour measurements.
Stop and retain the current viewmodel package if the repair would require editing, splitting, or compensating inside its materialized component root instead of using product-owned bindings.
Do not claim completion from scripted state mutation, diagnostic teleportation, or settled screenshots without ordinary-input and uninterrupted-mission evidence.

strategy.rationale: Use explicit gameplay-gated raw input ownership and deterministic full-roster spatial reservations. This materially differs from the four prior progression treatments by repairing event delivery and invalid-slot fallback directly, while the viewmodel work stays in the product-owned controller instead of retuning or replacing preserved asset internals.

code: Run the frozen clean-boot validation and require zero script parse, missing-resource, or startup errors.
Inspect the input path for one owner per look/ADS edge, explicit gameplay-state gating, right-stick mappings, and no dependence on GUI unhandled delivery.
Check roster initialization deterministically rejects invalid reservations, creates exactly 18 unique IDs in 3/5/10 regions, and preserves restore serialization.
Verify no file beneath the materialized viewmodel component root changed and all product-specific binding remains in candidate-owned controller or scene files.
runtime: Tester starts through the ordinary shell, records yaw/pitch before and after mouse plus right-stick look, and confirms pause/resume and terminal boundaries suppress and restore input correctly.
Tester completes one fresh uninterrupted A→B→C run, observing 3/5/10 activation, eliminations, capture/key commits, route unlocks, and Charlie availability without diagnostic state mutation.

At fresh spawn and during each active region, capture roster telemetry and require every pair to remain outside combined capsule radii with no overlap, prolonged deadlock, or invalid reservation fallback.

From identical gameplay framing, hold and release ADS on each weapon and capture authoritative state plus settled transforms, then exercise fire/recovery, reload, switch, pause, and checkpoint restore transitions.
visual: Capture matched hip and settled-ADS frames for AK-74M and Saiga-12; sights must visibly align toward the reticle with stable hands, sockets, roots, and unobstructed environment visibility.
Capture representative fire peak/recovery, reload contact, and switch frames from the shipped first-person camera; each state must be visually distinct and consistent with runtime authority.

Capture first-person and overhead diagnostic views at early, middle, and contested moments in Alpha, Bravo, and Charlie to confirm distributed actors, visible movement/telegraphs, and collision-free spacing.
Re-run the frozen combat-readability animation-motion and enemy-combat-AI reviews, with GameLoop Runtime and Tester owning evidence recapture, issue closure, and final verdicts.

done_when: Ordinary relative mouse input changes authoritative yaw and pitch while gameplay is enabled, and equivalent right-stick actions provide bounded frame-rate-independent look.
Title, briefing, pause, terminal, death, and result states reject gameplay look input; capture and release transitions cannot leave internal mouse state inconsistent with the viewport.

All 18 stable identities receive deterministic navigation-resolved initial reservations whose pairwise distances exceed their combined collision footprint; no failed search may return an occupied primary point.
Alpha, Bravo, and Charlie activate in 3/5/10 order during one uninterrupted A→B→C run, with route locks and capture ownership advancing only from authoritative mission state.

Early, middle, and contested telemetry exposes actor ID, region, route slot, position, velocity, action, avoidance state, and nearest-neighbour distance without disturbing the preserved Alpha combat state machine.
Checkpoint restore retains each actor identity, reserved position, alive/ammo/activation state, and the existing atomic 18-actor transaction.
tasks.instructions: Replace the repeated transform-oriented progression treatment with explicit gameplay input ownership: consume mouse motion and mapped right-stick look through a single authoritative, state-gated path that remains independent of GUI handled-state, with receipts sufficient to compare injected deltas to yaw/pitch changes. Repair roster placement as a deterministic reservation transaction using navigation-projected positions and real capsule separation; never return an already-invalid primary projection when sampling fails. Preserve the authored map, existing 18 identities, region counts, Alpha AI behavior, avoidance integration, and checkpoint transaction. Expose bounded diagnostics needed for Tester to verify ordinary-input A→B→C progression and separation without adding debug-only progression shortcuts.
tasks.title: Restore ordinary aim and collision-free enemy progression

done_when: A normal right-mouse press, hold, and release produces authoritative hip→ADS→hip edges and a settled ADS transform clearly distinct from the hip baseline.
Both AK-74M and Saiga-12 align their sighting surface toward the reticle in ADS without clipping, hand separation, socket drift, root instability, or changes inside the materialized component.
ADS is cancelled or restored consistently across fire, reload, inspect, weapon switch, pause, death, deployment, and checkpoint restore according to the authoritative interrupt order.

Runtime state reports the input edge, requested aim state, actual viewmodel aim state, transition completion, active weapon/profile, and current transform so a visual pose cannot disagree silently with authority.

Representative fire/recovery, tactical reload, and weapon-switch motion remains readable from the shipped first-person camera for both weapons while preserving ammunition, shot, and equipped-weapon authority.
tasks.instructions: Repair ADS as a product-owned input and animation-binding path in the weapon controller, using the same gameplay gating and ordered edge handling as the authoritative weapon actions. Verify the controller drives the already-bound intact hands-and-weapon instance and observes completion instead of assuming that a requested state rendered correctly. Keep all framing and transition coordination outside the materialized viewmodel component root; do not replace, split, or edit the preserved package. Make hip, settled ADS, fire/recovery, reload, and switch states observable for matched runtime recapture on both weapons.
